Barzillai
bar-ZIL-eye
proper noun (Old Testament figure)
Barzillai (Hebrew Barzillay) means "man of iron," from barzel, iron; he was a wealthy Gileadite of Rogelim.

📖 Biblical Definition

Barzillai the Gileadite was a very great and aged man who sustained King David in the hour of his flight, when Absalom had usurped the throne and the king passed over Jordan to Mahanaim. With Shobi and Machir, Barzillai brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, with wheat, barley, flour, parched corn, beans, lentils, honey, butter, sheep, and cheese, that the king and his weary people might eat in the wilderness. This was no small loyalty, for to aid the rejected king when his cause seemed lost was to hazard all. When David was restored and would have brought Barzillai over Jordan to feed him in Jerusalem and reward his faithfulness with a place at the royal table, the old man, fourscore years of age, modestly declined, saying he could no longer discern good from evil nor taste what he ate and drank, and asked only to die in his own city by the grave of his father and mother. He sent Chimham his servant in his stead. Here is a portrait of faithful old age: liberal in giving, humble in receiving, content with little, and mindful of mortality and the grave. David remembered him to the last, charging Solomon to show kindness to the sons of Barzillai and let them be of those that eat at his table, for so he had stood by the king in his distress.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The aged and wealthy Gileadite who provisioned David in his flight from Absalom and humbly declined a place at the royal table.

expand to see more

BARZILLAI, proper noun. From the Hebrew, "man of iron"; a great man of Gilead dwelling in Rogelim.

The host who supplied David and his people at Mahanaim in their distress.

An example of faithful, liberal, and self-effacing old age.

As it is written, "I am this day fourscore years old: and can I discern between good and evil?" (2 Sam 19:35).

Remembered by David to the last, who charged Solomon to show kindness to his sons.

📖 Key Scripture

2Sa 17:27 — "And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,"

2Sa 19:32 — "Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he was a very great man."

2Sa 19:35 — "I am this day fourscore years old: and can I discern between good and evil? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? wherefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?"

1Ki 2:7 — "But shew kindness unto the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at thy table: for so they came to me when I fled because of Absalom thy brother."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Barzillai faces no postmodern redefinition, but his example of honored, generous, godly old age is much neglected in an age that prizes youth.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The biblical principle to recover is the honor and grace of faithful old age. Barzillai, fourscore years old, did not grasp at the comforts and dignities the king offered, but gave liberally in the day of trouble and asked only to die near the graves of his parents. An age that idolizes youth and dreads aging needs the steady iron faith of this Gileadite.

To recover Barzillai's example is to learn contentment, hospitality, and a sober mindfulness of death. He served the rejected king at great risk, sought no reward, and trusted his sons to the kindness of the crown. So the believer is taught to spend himself in love, to hold honors loosely, and to face the grave with the calm of one who has been faithful in his generation.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The account is rooted in the loyalty shown to David in the rebellion of Absalom and in the godly conduct of the aged.

expand to see more

Absalom's revolt drove David across Jordan to Mahanaim (2 Sam 17).

Barzillai, with Shobi and Machir, brought abundant provision to the king (2 Sam 17:27-29).

After the victory David offered Barzillai a place in Jerusalem (2 Sam 19:33).

The old man declined, sending Chimham in his stead (2 Sam 19:37-38).

David's dying charge to Solomon secured kindness for Barzillai's sons (1 Kgs 2:7).

Usage

"Barzillai is cited as the model of generous and self-forgetful old age."

"His confession that he could no longer taste or hear is quoted on the frailties of age."

"His name marks loyalty to the LORD's anointed in the day of adversity."
